title: Technology Sector Update for 08/30/2018: SMTC,EA,AAPL,HEI
text:

Technology stocks were falling in late trade, reversing small gains from earlier in Thursday trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were losing over 0.4% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was slipping slightly more than 1.0%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Semtech ( SMTC ) rode a more than 16% advance on Thursday to its best share price since August 2000 at $58 apiece after the analog and mixed-signal chipmaker reported non-GAAP Q2 net income and revenue beating Wall Street expectations and prompting analysts at Oppenheimer to raise their price target for the company's stock by $7 to $65 a share. Excluding one-time items, Semtech earned $0.55 per share during the three months ended July 29, topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.01 per share. Revenue rose to $163.21 million from $153.13 million a year ago, also exceeding the $161.21 million estimate. Needham & Co Thursday also increased its price target for Semtech by $5 to $60 a share.
In other sector news:
(+) Apple ( AAPL ) was almost 1% higher during Thursday trading following reports it purchased Akonia Holographics, a startup company specializing in making waveguide lenses - thin, transparent smart glass lenses that display vibrant, full-color, wide field-of-view images - for augmented reality glasses. Akonia owns over 200 patents in the holographic space and may see the acquisition as a sign Apple is venturing into the consumer AR headset business, according to a Reuters report. Neither Apple nor Akonia would comment on the transaction. Financial terms and other details also were not disclosed.
(-) Heico ( HEI ) was trading lower Thursday, dropping almost 1% to reverse a like-sized advance earlier in the session that followed the electronic components manufacturer saying it has acquired 100% of the business and assets of privately held Optical Display Engineering. Financial terms of the all-cash transaction were not disclosed, although Heico said its expects the deal will add to its per-share earnings during the first year after closing.
(-) Electronic Arts ( EA ) retreated Thursday, at one point falling over 9%, after it reduced its outlook for FY19 net bookings by about $350 million to around $5.2 billion, in part to reflect a four-week delay in the upcoming launch of its highly-anticipated 'Battlefield V' video game. The game will be released on Nov. 20 instead of Oct. 23, the company said in a statement, explaining the later date will allow it "to deliver the best possible experience for gamers." It also said about $115 million - or roughly one-third - of the lower expected bookings this year was driven by recent changes n foreign exchange rates.
